Subject: FinPay discovery recap + next steps (cost/TCO tests)

Hi Sarah / Devon

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard from FinPay:
- Primary workload: customer service assistants + fraud triage snippets (short context, mixed LLM generate + embed lookups).
- QPS profile: bursty during business hours, avg sustained ~25 rps, peaks around ~120 rps for sub-second flows.
- Latency SLO: ~<200ms p50 for short completion calls (50-150 tokens).
- Key evaluation asks: clear unit economics (per-1M tokens), impact of batching and caching on unit cost and latency, and direct comparisons vs Bedrock/OpenAI for both cost and performance.

Proposed test matrix (from our side):
1) Baseline: 1M token run, no batching, no prefix cache (measure latency, throughput, cost).
2) Batching: simulate 16-concurrent batching policy for 1M tokens equivalent load (estimate throughput gain and per-token cost).
3) Cache: prefix/KV cache scenario with a 60% cache-hit assumption for repeated prompts (measure token reduction and end-to-end latency).

Deliverables we propose:
- Estimated per-1M token costs for Redwood, Bedrock (customer-configured instance), and OpenAI using the same model family baseline.
- Expected unit economics under batching and cache-hit scenarios (spreadsheet attached).
- A short runbook for initial canary tests + temporary creds for smoke testing.

Attachments: finpay_requirements.pdf (your doc), redwood_cost_model_v1.xlsx (our cost calc), redwood_test_matrix.md (planned tests).

Can you confirm the QPS/latency assumptions above and whether you want us to include GPU instance pricing for Bedrock or just SaaS API list prices?

If that looks good, Marcus (cc'd) will own the test plan and we can provision canary access early next week.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya

Confirmed on the profile; that aligns closely with what we expect. A couple of clarifying items:
- For Bedrock, please include both managed API list prices and a rough on-demand EC2/GPU instance-based estimate (we run heavy steady-state jobs and want to compare both models).
- For OpenAI, please use the closest equivalent model family we discussed and note any differences in context-window economics.
- For caching: 60% is a reasonable starting assumption, but can you also run a 40%/80% sensitivity in the spreadsheet?

Also we care about tail latency (95th) for our fraud flows. If batching helps cost but increases p95 beyond 400ms that's a non-starter. Please call out latency tradeoffs clearly.

Can you share the test matrix and provisioning steps by Monday? If possible, give us temporary canary keys so our infra team can run one small smoke load.

Appreciate it
Sarah
VP Product, FinPay

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@finpay.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinPay discovery recap + next steps (cost/TCO tests)

Sarah

Thanks for the notes. Attached is the detailed test matrix and an initial cost model (redwood_cost_model_v1.xlsx). High-level numbers and assumptions below (ballpark estimates to guide the test plan):

Assumptions:
- Baseline model parity: Redwood-medium == Bedrock-equivalent-M; OpenAI-equivalent used for public SaaS pricing comparisons.
- Tokenization: 1M tokens = ~750-900k words depending on language mix; we'll normalize to tokens for cost line items.
- Target workload: 50k req/day (~unless you confirm otherwise), but we'll run a 1M-token equivalent run for unit economics.

Estimated per-1M-token cost (generation + minimal context inference; excludes long-term storage & support):
- Redwood (optimized runtime, batching & cache enabled where possible): $1.25 / 1M tokens
- AWS Bedrock (managed API, typical instance mix): $2.80 / 1M tokens (API list price estimate)
- Bedrock (self-managed EC2 GPU equivalency): $1.90 / 1M tokens (estimate depends on instance amortization + infra ops)
- OpenAI (public API pricing comparable family): $4.75 / 1M tokens

Batching & cache impacts (expected):
- Batching (16x): reduces per-token compute by ~20-35% depending on sequence-length variance; however p95 latency increases by ~30-70ms on average in our measurements.
- Prefix/KV Cache (60% hit): effective generated token count reduces proportional to miss rate; at 60% hit we see end-user token-generation cost drop ~40-50% for repetitive flows. Cache introduces minimal added lookup latency (~5-20ms) but reduces total generation time when hit.

Tradeoffs:
- If you must keep p95 < 400ms for fraud flows, we recommend conservative batching (4-8) or dynamic batching by route and prioritizing those calls on low-latency nodes.
- For chat/customer-assist flows where p50 matters more, batching 16 and cache 60% is excellent for cost.

Planned tests (we can run these in a dedicated canary project):
A) Baseline single-shot 1M token run (no batching, no cache) measure p50/p95, throughput, raw cost.
B) Batching sweep (4, 8, 16) measure cost delta and p95 impact.
C) Cache-hit sweep (40%, 60%, 80%) measure effective token reduction and end-to-end latency.
D) Bedrock/OpenAI parity runs same prompt-set to compare latencies and per-token billing.

Next steps:
- We'll provision a canary project and share temporary keys + runbook Monday morning.
- Monica will coordinate infra access; Neha will help validate telemetry hooks for p95.

Open items for FinPay: please confirm the daily request volume (or a representative sample), and whether you want us to include the EC2 instance amortization model for Bedrock in the shared sheet.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_cost_model_v1.xlsx, redwood_test_matrix.md
